subject: ela
intro: Opinion writing means telling what you think and giving a reason why. A good opinion sentence has three parts: an opinion word (I think / I believe), the topic, and a reason using the word 'because.' In Grade 1, writers also add a closing sentence to wrap up their thinking.

items.prompt: A student wants to write her opinion about dogs and cats. She writes: 'Dogs are better.' Is this a complete opinion sentence? How can she make it better?

steps: A complete opinion sentence needs an opinion word, a topic, and a reason.
'Dogs are better' has the topic (dogs) but no opinion word and no reason.
Add an opinion word at the start: 'I think dogs are better.'
Add a reason using 'because': 'I think dogs are better because they like to play outside.'
solution.answer: I think dogs are better pets than cats because they like to play outside.

items.prompt: A student writes: 'I think pizza is the best food because it has cheese and I love cheese.' Does this sentence have all three parts of a good opinion sentence?

steps: Check for an opinion word: 'I think' — yes.
Check for the topic: 'pizza is the best food' — yes.
Check for a reason: 'because it has cheese and I love cheese' — yes.
This sentence has all three parts. It is a strong opinion sentence.
solution.answer: Yes. The sentence has an opinion word ('I think'), a topic ('pizza is the best food'), and a reason ('because it has cheese'). It is a complete opinion sentence.

items.prompt:
Read this opinion paragraph:

'I think we should have more recess. Recess is fun. We get to run and play. That is why more recess is a good idea.'

What is the opinion? What is one reason given?

steps: The opinion is the writer's main thought: 'We should have more recess.'
The reason supports the opinion: 'Recess is fun' and 'We get to run and play.'
The closing sentence wraps it up: 'That is why more recess is a good idea.'
solution.answer: The opinion is that we should have more recess. One reason is that recess is fun because students get to run and play.

items.prompt: A student is asked: 'Do you think reading or math is more important?' She is not sure how to start. How should she begin her opinion sentence?

steps: Decide which one you think is more important.
Start with an opinion word: 'I think' or 'I believe.'
Name the topic: 'reading is more important.'
Add a reason with 'because': 'because books help you learn about everything.'
solution.answer: I think reading is more important because books help you learn about everything.

items.prompt: A student writes: 'Summer is the best season. I think so because you can swim and there is no school. Summer is really great.' Which sentence is the opinion? Which is the closing?

steps: The first sentence states the main opinion: 'Summer is the best season.'
The middle sentence gives a reason: 'I think so because you can swim and there is no school.'
The last sentence is the closing: 'Summer is really great.' It wraps up the writing.
solution.answer: The opinion is 'Summer is the best season.' The closing sentence is 'Summer is really great.'

items.prompt:
Finish this opinion sentence with a reason:

'I think cats make great pets because _____.'

Write a reason that tells why cats are great.
items.hint: Think about something nice that cats do, like purring or being soft.

steps: Think of one good thing about cats.
Start your reason after the word 'because.'
Make sure the reason connects to why cats are great pets.
solution.answer: I think cats make great pets because they are soft and they purr when you pet them.

items.prompt: Do you think it is better to eat lunch inside or outside? Write a complete opinion sentence using 'I think' and 'because.'
items.hint: Pick one choice. Then think of ONE reason why it is better.

steps: Choose inside or outside.
Start with 'I think.'
State which is better.
Add 'because' and a reason.
solution.answer: I think it is better to eat lunch outside because the fresh air makes the food taste better.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence: 'I like apples.'

Rewrite it as a complete opinion sentence with an opinion word and a reason.
items.hint: Add 'I think' and then add 'because' with a reason at the end.

steps: Start with an opinion word: 'I think.'
Keep the topic: 'apples are the best fruit.'
Add a reason: 'because they are sweet and crunchy.'
solution.answer: I think apples are the best fruit because they are sweet and crunchy.

items.prompt: Write 2-3 sentences about whether you think it is better to have a big dog or a small dog. Include your opinion, one reason, and a closing sentence.
items.hint: Sentence 1: your opinion. Sentence 2: your reason. Sentence 3: a wrap-up like 'That is why I think...'

steps: Sentence 1 states the opinion: 'I think small dogs are better.'
Sentence 2 gives a reason: 'They are easy to hold and they fit in small homes.'
Sentence 3 closes: 'That is why I would choose a small dog.'
solution.answer: I think small dogs are better pets. They are easy to hold and fit in small homes. That is why I would choose a small dog.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: 'I believe art class is fun. Kids can paint and draw. Everyone should have art class.'

Does this paragraph have an opinion, a reason, and a closing? Explain.
items.hint: Read each sentence and decide: is it an opinion, a reason, or a closing?

steps: Sentence 1: 'I believe art class is fun.' This is the opinion.
Sentence 2: 'Kids can paint and draw.' This is the reason.
Sentence 3: 'Everyone should have art class.' This is the closing.
Yes, the paragraph has all three parts.
solution.answer: Yes. The opinion is 'art class is fun.' The reason is 'kids can paint and draw.' The closing is 'everyone should have art class.'
